note: Role of every reference case in the discovery programme. training = the case contributed to the rules and may be cited as a positive; held_back = the case must not be used to change a rule, the search space or the ranking; negative = a corpus that only measures false positives. Burned cases stay in the file: hiding that a test has been seen would make later recall numbers meaningless.  S1.9 source handoff: the answer payloads of the held_back entries were redacted; the entries stay so that the leak checks and the blind-claim accounting still see them.

references.burned_reason: S1.2c reconstructed the family by hand and S1.2d made the D7 rule find it from the extended entry set; it can no longer serve as a blind test, only as a regression anchor.
references.root_cause: 4-byte file-descriptor number compared against a caller supplied value; the number can be reused by a different object, so the matched record does not own the reference that is dropped twice

references.burned_reason: integrated exploit family (families.json) whose shape informed D1/D4; D1/D4 are still gated untrusted, so the case is a training reference and not a positive control.

A non-terminating predecessor-cycle defect and a path reconstruction defect were then repaired, so the S1.3 freeze was invalidated after the result was known. Afterglow is now a regression/negative control only; no rule was tuned to its root cause.

references.note: false-positive denominator over functions whose correction is independently established, not over the firmware as a whole. A function that is merely unlabelled is UNKNOWN, never a true negative: the same firmware carries a positive ReLapse case, so 'FW 13.52 is negative' is not a defensible label.
